Marc: Heads-up — planning a rolling schema migration for events.user_events_v2 at 02:00 UTC (today). It adds device_id (nullable) and a new composite index. This will require a brief write lock during the index swap, estimate ~90s. Plan pasted below.
Anya: Can we avoid a global write lock? What about the ingesters that write concurrently?
Marc: Plan: 1) deploy migration code with feature flag off (safe) 2) run async backfill in batches into the new column (no writes blocked) 3) perform controlled index swap (brief WRITE lock) 4) flip feature flag -> switch traffic to new index. Backfill runs on workers against replicas. Only the index swap needs a short lock.
Dan: Backfill workers must be pinned to a known image to keep batching deterministic. I'll pin to the latest tested tag. If autoscaler brings newer images with different chunking we risk long backfill times.
Ryan: What was the swap time on staging? Need a guardrail for rollback.
Marc: Staging run last night: ~70s for a 1B-row partitioned shard. Prod expected 60–120s depending on IO. We'll put a 02:00-02:30 change window and pre-warm replicas + run on low-traffic hour.
Leah: Suggest explicit rollback criteria: if WRITE lock exceeds 150s OR p99 write latency > 200ms for 2 consecutive minutes -> abort swap and restore old index. Add a deploy-bot rollback hook and runbook steps.
deploy-bot: CI checks green. Migration SQL approved. Deploy gated: manual=true. Runbook link: https://go/infra/playbooks/migration-events-v2
sre-ops: We'll enable canary rate limiting on ingesters to 10% traffic for the migrated codepath during rollout. Also will divert background low-priority writes to secondary queue during the swap.
Anya: Analytics team reads the new column for derived metrics during their backfill — we need a compatibility contract and a brief validation window. @analytics-team FYI.
Dan: Contract note added to the PR. Analytics will run compatibility job in sandbox 01:30-01:50 and confirm.
Marc: Quick abort commands and snippets below. Keep these handy during the window.
Marc: ```sql
-- controlled swap (example)
BEGIN;
ALTER TABLE events DROP INDEX IF EXISTS ix_events_old;
ALTER TABLE events ADD INDEX ix_events_new (device_id, created_at);
COMMIT;
-- rollback (recreate old index if swap fails)
```
Marc: Deploy/backfill helpers:```bash
# run migration (blocking guard timeout)
./bin/migrate --env=prod --name=events_device_id --timeout=600
# async backfill (run before swap, parallel workers)
./bin/backfill --table=events --col=device_id --batch-size=5000 --workers=8
```
Leah: I'll own monitoring and the runbook edits. I'll set alerts: lock_duration > 120s, write_p99 > 200ms, replication_lag > 5s. I'll also send a calendar invite for 01:45 pre-check.
Ryan: I'll pin worker image in infra manifest: image: redwood/workers:2026.03.19 and open a PR for infra rollout.
Anya: Sounds good. :eyes:
sre-ops: We'll post heartbeat updates to #incidents during the window and escalate to oncall if error spike or alert fires. We'll also have DB grep logs ready: `tail -n 200 /var/log/mysql/error.log` and a fast rollback script on the bastion.
Marc: TL;DR: migration at 02:00 UTC, expected ~90s lock, rollback criteria defined, worker image pinned, canary on ingesters, analytics compatibility check. Everyone OK with the plan?
Dan: ack :thumbsup:
Leah: ack :thumbsup:
Ryan: ack
Anya: ack
deploy-bot: Scheduled deploy window created; manual gate required at index-swap step.
sre-ops: We'll be watching. Posting check-in at 01:50 and then at start/finish.
